frames.text: Herevale. Your world. Ten thousand years of songs, harvests, quarrels, and quiet evenings under a sky whose stars all pointed one direction — coreward, toward the Pillar.
They arrived without demands. The Wake does not negotiate with worlds it has already judged. A hull the size of a mountain range slid down through the noon sky, and the light changed.
It took them one day. The songs, the harvests, the quiet evenings — burned to glass. You remember the roads out of the city most: everyone running, and the sky too bright behind them.

Whoever had a hull that could hold air ran for open sky. Not all of them made it out of the gravity well. You watched the flashes from a freight rack in a battered survey ship, engines screaming, and stopped counting.
Ahead, on every horizon, stands the Pillar of Stars — the burning column of the galactic core. Every myth your people ever told points down that road. Now it is the only road you have left.

Every schoolchild in the arm knows the Ancients. An alien race that vanished tens of thousands of years ago, leaving ruins on a hundred worlds and not one body, not one answer. For centuries, scientists, pilgrims, and treasure fleets have gone coreward to learn what became of them. They found ruins. Only ever more ruins. No revelation has ever come back from the Pillar.

So when your blind jump ends at a nameless, empty world wearing Ancient stonework — it should mean nothing. Signals like the one threading up through this dust have swallowed ten thousand lifetimes and given back dirt. But standing at the rim of the dig, listening to something patient still broadcasting far below... you know it. In your gut. This time is different.
